tools.name: shop_info
tools.description: What this shop is, who runs it, how delivery, payment and returns work.

tools.name: list_products
tools.description: Every product on sale, with price, stock and a one-line summary.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Everything the shop says about one product: the label's amounts, how to take it, price, pictures.

tools.name: search_products
tools.description: Search the shop the way a customer would ask, in Thai or English — an ingredient, a concern, a brand.

tools.name: get_reviews
tools.description: Reviews customers left, for one product or the whole shop.

tools.name: start_checkout
tools.description: Put these items in the shop's cart and hand back the link that opens checkout. Nothing is charged and no account is needed — the customer pays as a guest, exactly as on the website. Use this for an ordinary purchase.

tools.name: create_payment_link
tools.description: Write a real pending order into the shop and return its pay page. Needs a token, because it puts a row in the shop's books; for an ordinary purchase use start_checkout instead.

tools.name: get_order_status
tools.description: Where an order has got to. Needs the order number and the email on it.

tools.name: usage_report
tools.description: What assistants have been asking this shop, and which questions it failed to answer.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_reviews, get_order_status · Private data: create_payment_link · Public sink: get_order_status.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_reviews, get_order_status · Private data: create_payment_link · Public sink: get_order_status

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
